proposals.before: Zhang Yin, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Field Office, composed the 《Poem on the Zhao Girl》.
proposals.after: Zhang Yin, Vice Director of the Bureau of Agricultural Colonies, composed the Poem on the Zhao Girl.
proposals.reason: 尚書屯田員外郎 is a Song yuanwailang of the agricultural-colonies bureau, not an Outer Gentleman of a Revenue field office; the title-markers around the poem title are also non-English.

proposals.before: Zhang Yin, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Field Office, composed the 《Poem on the Zhao Girl》.
proposals.after: Zhang Yin, Vice Director of the Bureau of Agricultural Colonies, composed the Poem on the Zhao Girl.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation as the idiomatic line: 屯田員外郎 is not Outer Gentleman of a Revenue field office.

proposals.before: Rong Shi was the younger sister of Rong.
proposals.after: Rong Shi was the younger sister of Ni.
proposals.reason: 薿 is the brother's given name Ni; rendering it as Rong fuses him with Rong Shi.

proposals.before: Rong Shi was the younger sister of Rong.
proposals.after: Rong Shi was the younger sister of Ni.
proposals.reason: 薿 is Ni, not a second Rong.

proposals.before: In the fifth year of Shaoxing Yingzhou suffered famine and bandits rose on Guanyin Mountain, raiding the countryside.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Yingzhou suffered famine and bandits rose on Guanyin Mountain, raiding the countryside.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses the era name Shaoxing with the place Yingzhou, obscuring that Shaoxing is the reign and Yingzhou the prefecture.

proposals.before: Zhang Wenrao, Commissioner of Judicial Review for the Chengdu Circuit, suspected Yang of having a secret affair and, fearing exposure, killed Yi to silence him; he ordered Shiquan Army to investigate.
proposals.after: Zhang Wenrao, Commissioner of Judicial Review for the Chengdu Circuit, suspected Yang of having a secret affair and, fearing exposure, of killing Yi to silence him; he ordered Shiquan Army to investigate.
proposals.reason: The literal English makes Zhang Wenrao the killer of Yi; the Chinese has Zhang suspecting that Yang killed Yi to silence him.

proposals.before: The investigating official Li Zhiyuan doubted the case; that evening he dressed in full regalia and prayed to Heaven.
proposals.after: The investigating official Li Zhining doubted the case; that evening he dressed in full regalia and prayed to Heaven.
proposals.reason: 李誌寧 is Li Zhining; Zhiyuan mismatches the character 寧.

proposals.before: The investigating official Li Zhiyuan doubted the case; in the evening he dressed in full regalia and prayed to Heaven.
proposals.after: The investigating official Li Zhining doubted the case; in the evening he dressed in full regalia and prayed to Heaven.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise romanizes 誌寧 as Zhiyuan instead of Zhining.

proposals.before: Zhiyuan reflected on the dream: "Is not the killer surnamed Yuan?"
proposals.after: Zhining reflected on the dream: "Is not the killer surnamed Yuan?"
proposals.reason: The given name 誌寧 continues as Zhiyuan; it should remain Zhining.

proposals.before: Zhiyuan thought to himself about the dream omen: "Is not the killer surnamed Yuan?"
proposals.after: Zhining thought to himself about the dream omen: "Is not the killer surnamed Yuan?"
proposals.reason: The literal English continues the wrong romanization Zhiyuan for 誌寧.

proposals.before: That same year the bandit Peng You raised Longquan in Jizhou; Li Sheng's wife Liang Shi, choosing righteousness over disgrace, drowned herself in the river.
proposals.after: That same year the bandit Peng You raided Longquan in Jizhou; Li Sheng's wife Liang Shi, choosing righteousness over disgrace, drowned herself in the river.
proposals.reason: Chinese 犯 means to invade or raid, not to raise a place; the literal already has raided.

proposals.before: During the Shaoding era bandits overran Ninghua County; officials all fled. Huang Kun, magistrate of Jiangle, organized local strongmen Wang Wanquan and Wang Lun to rally the stockades against the bandits; Yan was foremost in supplying troops and grain, and many enemies were killed or captured.
proposals.after: During the Shaoding era bandits overran Ninghua County; officials all fled. Huang Fou, magistrate of Jiangle, organized local strongmen Wang Wanquan and Wang Lun to rally the stockades against the bandits; Yan was foremost in supplying troops and grain, and many enemies were killed or captured.
proposals.reason: The personal name 垺 is Fou/Pou, not Kun; the idiomatic English invents Kun.

proposals.before: During Jianyan Wang Mao supervised the wine tax at Shanggao; when Jin troops invaded Yun, he abandoned his post and fled, Zhao accompanying him.
proposals.after: During Jianyan, Wang Mao supervised the wine tax at Shanggao; when Jin troops invaded Yun, he abandoned his post and fled, Zhao accompanying him.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the reign name Jianyan with the personal name Wang Mao.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Shaoxing bandits rose and drove her into Huangshan Temple. They pressed her and she would not yield; they placed a blade to her neck and shouted: 'You are mere rat thieves—your lives are like mayflies; I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I suffer your disgrace!
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Shaoxing bandits rose and drove her into Huangshan Temple. They pressed her and she would not yield; they placed a blade to her neck. She shouted: 'You are mere rat thieves—your lives are like mayflies; I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I suffer your disgrace!
proposals.reason: The quoted speech insults the bandits in the first person as a respectable daughter; 叱曰 is her rebuke, not the bandits speaking.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Shaoxing bandits rose; she was driven into Huangshan Temple. The bandits pressed her and she would not yield; they placed a blade to her neck and shouted: 'You lot are rat thieves—your lives are like mayflies; I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I suffer your disgrace!
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Shaoxing bandits rose; she was driven into Huangshan Temple. The bandits pressed her and she would not yield; they placed a blade to her neck. She shouted: 'You lot are rat thieves—your lives are like mayflies; I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I suffer your disgrace!
proposals.reason: Same misattribution: the first-person rebuke belongs to Chen Shi, not to the bandits.

proposals.before: Later her husband and mother-in-law both died, leaving a young son; her parents wished to remarry her. Hou said: 'Through a lowly woman's body my son was fortunate to enter a worthy household—how could I leave and leave the Xie clan without posterity?
proposals.after: Later her husband and mother-in-law both died, leaving a young son; her parents wished to remarry her. Hou said: 'I, a lowly woman, was fortunate to marry into the household of a worthy recluse—how could I leave and leave the Xie clan without posterity?
proposals.reason: 兒 is the speaker's humble first person, not 兒 as son; 歸隱居賢者之門 is her marriage into Xie Bi's house.

proposals.before: Later her husband and mother-in-law both died, leaving a young son; her parents wished to marry her off again. Hou said: 'My son, through a lowly woman's body, was fortunate to enter the gate of a reclusive worthy—how could I leave and leave the Xie clan without posterity?
proposals.after: Later her husband and mother-in-law both died, leaving a young son; her parents wished to marry her off again. Hou said: 'I, a lowly woman, was fortunate to marry into the gate of a reclusive worthy—how could I leave and leave the Xie clan without posterity?
proposals.reason: 兒以賤婦人 is self-reference; the English makes the son the subject of 歸賢者之門.

proposals.before: Commander Wu of the military household, judging Fangde a heroic figure and fearing he might incite rebellion, offered a reward for his capture and rooted out his entire family.
proposals.after: Wanhu Wu, judging Fangde a heroic figure and fearing he might incite rebellion, offered a reward for his capture and rooted out his entire family.
proposals.reason: 萬戶 is the Yuan myriarch office title, not 'of the military household'.

proposals.before: During Deyou she followed the Huai garrison at Yingshu Ford.
proposals.after: During Deyou she followed Zhao Huai, who was garrisoning Yishu Dam.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從淮戍銀樹埧 means she accompanied Zhao Huai while he garrisoned 銀樹埧 (an embankment), not a Huai garrison at Yingshu Ford.

proposals.before: During Deyou she followed the Huai garrison at Yingshu Ford.
proposals.after: During Deyou she followed Huai, who was garrisoning Yishu Dam.
proposals.reason: Same 淮/埧 misreading: 淮 is Zhao Huai and 埧 is a dam, not a ford.

proposals.before: Zhao, wife of the Tan clanswoman, was from Yongxin in Jizhou.
proposals.after: Zhao, a wife of the Tan family, was from Yongxin in Jizhou.
proposals.reason: 譚氏婦趙 names Zhao as a married woman of the Tan household, not the wife of a Tan clanswoman.

proposals.before: Zhao, wife of the Tan clanswoman, was a native of Yongxin in Ji Prefecture.
proposals.after: Zhao, a wife of the Tan family, was a native of Yongxin in Ji Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Same inversion of 譚氏婦趙 as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Yuan troops took the city. Zhao, holding her infant, hid with her uncle and mother-in-law in the district school but was seized by brutal soldiers who killed her uncle and mother-in-law. They seized Zhao and tried to violate her; she refused. They threatened her with blades: 'Follow me and live; refuse and die.'
proposals.after: Yuan troops took the city. Zhao, holding her infant, hid with her father-in-law and mother-in-law in the district school but was seized by brutal soldiers who killed her father-in-law and mother-in-law. They seized Zhao and tried to violate her; she refused. They threatened her with blades: 'Follow me and live; refuse and die.'
proposals.reason: In the 舅、姑 pair of a married woman's biography, 舅 is the father-in-law, not an uncle.

proposals.before: Zhao cursed: 'My uncle died by your hand, my mother-in-law by your hand—I would rather die with them than live in unrighteousness.'
proposals.after: Zhao cursed: 'My father-in-law died by your hand, my mother-in-law by your hand—I would rather die with them than live in unrighteousness.'
proposals.reason: Same 舅、姑 in-law pair as the preceding sentence.

proposals.before: Old woman Lin was from Yongchun and came of age unmarried.
proposals.after: The Lin girl was from Yongchun and came of age unmarried.
proposals.reason: 林老女 with 及笄未婚 is an unmarried daughter come of age, not an aged woman.

proposals.before: The old woman of the Lin family was a native of Yongchun; she came of age unmarried.
proposals.after: The unmarried Lin daughter was a native of Yongchun; she came of age unmarried.
proposals.reason: Same error: 老女 here is the unmarried girl, not an old woman.

proposals.before: The daughter of the Han clan, styled Ximeng, was a native of Baling—or said to be a descendant of Chancellor Qi.
proposals.after: The daughter of the Han clan, styled Ximeng, was a native of Baling—or said to be a descendant of Chancellor Han Qi.
proposals.reason: 丞相琦 is Han Qi; the literal drops the surname.

proposals.before: Liang, wife of the Wang clanswoman, was from Linchuan.
proposals.after: Liang, wife of a Wang clansman, was from Linchuan.
proposals.reason: 王氏婦梁 names Liang as wife of a Wang-clan husband, née Liang, not the wife of a Wang clanswoman.

proposals.before: Liang, wife of the Wang clanswoman, was a native of Linchuan.
proposals.after: Liang, wife of a Wang clansman, was a native of Linchuan.
proposals.reason: The literal English repeats the same reversed kinship: 王氏婦 is the wife of a Wang-clan man.

proposals.before: Years later, childless, he planned to remarry but could not agree on a match, so he told his wife's story. That night he dreamed she said: 'After my death I was reborn in a certain clan; I am now ten.'
proposals.after: Years later, childless, he planned to remarry but could not agree on a match, so he told this to his former wife. That night he dreamed she said: 'After my death I was reborn in a certain clan; I am now ten.'
proposals.reason: 告其故妻 means he addressed his deceased wife, not that he recounted her story to others.

proposals.before: In the second year of Duanping Vice General Rong Quan rebelled and held the city; the Commissioner sent a Martial Wing Gentleman to summon him.
proposals.after: In the second year of Duanping, Vice General Rong Quan rebelled and held the city; the Commissioner sent someone offering the rank of Martial Wing Gentleman to summon him.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses the reign date with Vice General and treats 武翼郎 as the envoy rather than a rank used to summon Rong Quan.

decisions.reason: 尚書屯田員外郎 is the vice director of the agricultural-colonies bureau, not an outer gentleman of a Revenue field office; dropping the title-markers around 趙女詩 is also correct English.

decisions.reason: The literal line repeats the same false office; 屯田員外郎 is not a Ministry of Revenue field post.
薿 is the brother's given name; calling him Rong wrongly identifies him with 榮氏.
The literal likewise substitutes Rong for 薿; Ni is the correct given name.
Without the comma, 紹興五年 and 英州 fuse into one place-name; Shaoxing is the reign and Yingzhou the prefecture.
The original makes Zhang the killer; 疑楊有私，懼為人知，殺乙以滅口 is Zhang's suspicion that Yang killed Yi to hide an affair.

decisions.reason: 李誌寧 romanizes as Li Zhining; Zhiyuan does not match 寧.
The literal repeats Zhiyuan for 誌寧; Zhining is required.
The anaphor 誌寧 must stay Zhining, not Zhiyuan.
The literal continues the same false romanization of 誌寧.
犯吉州龍泉 means the bandit raided Longquan; raised invents a different action.
將樂縣宰黃垺 is Huang Fou; Kun is not a reading of 垺.
建炎中 is the Jianyan era, syntactically separate from 袤; the missing comma fuses reign and personal name.

decisions.reason: 兒以賤婦人 is Hou's humble self-reference; 歸隱居賢者之門 is her marriage into Xie Bi's house, not her son's.

decisions.after: Myriarch Wu, judging Fangde a heroic figure and fearing he might incite rebellion, offered a reward for his capture and rooted out his entire family.
decisions.reason: 萬戶 is the Yuan myriarch title, not a military household, but Wanhu Wu is not natural English; Myriarch Wu keeps the office and the surname 武.
從淮戍銀樹埧 means she accompanied Zhao Huai at Yishu Dam; 淮 is the man, 埧 an embankment, not a Huai garrison at a ford.
The literal repeats the Huai-garrison and ford errors; 淮 is Huai and 埧 is a dam.
譚氏婦趙 is Zhao, a married woman of the Tan house, not the wife of a Tan clanswoman.
The literal inverts the same 氏婦 formula; Zhao married into the Tan family.
In this married woman's 舅、姑 pair, 舅 is her father-in-law, not an uncle.
吾舅……吾姑 continues the same in-law pair; father-in-law is required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吾舅死於汝，吾姑又死於汝

decisions.reason: 及笄未婚 shows 林老女 is an unmarried girl come of age, not an old woman.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 林老女，永春人，及笄未婚

decisions.reason: The literal's old woman contradicts 及笄未婚; she is the unmarried Lin daughter.

decisions.reason: 王氏婦梁 is Liang, wife of a Wang-clan man, not the wife of a Wang clanswoman.

告其故妻 means he addressed his deceased wife; it is not recounting her story to others.
